title: NEET UG — Zoology | Urine Formation Filtration Reabsorption
description: Subject-wise test on Urine Formation Filtration Reabsorption (Zoology) for NEET UG. 50Q.
subject: neet-zoology
instructions: Section B: Attempt any 10 out of 15 questions
Correct answer: +4 marks | Wrong answer: -1 mark

questions.question: Which part of the nephron is primarily responsible for the ultrafiltration of blood, forming the glomerular filtrate?

options.explanation: The Loop of Henle is involved in reabsorption and concentration of urine, not ultrafiltration.
The PCT is involved in reabsorption of essential substances from the filtrate, not ultrafiltration.
Bowman's capsule, along with the glomerulus, forms the renal corpuscle, the site of ultrafiltration.
The collecting duct is involved in the final concentration of urine, not ultrafiltration.

questions.explanation: Bowman's capsule, along with the glomerulus, forms the renal corpuscle, which is the site of ultrafiltration. Blood is filtered from the glomerular capillaries into the Bowman's capsule. The Loop of Henle, PCT, and collecting duct are involved in reabsorption and secretion, not primary ultrafiltration.
questions.hint: This structure surrounds the glomerulus and collects the filtrate.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: During urine formation, which of the following substances is almost completely reabsorbed from the glomerular filtrate under normal physiological conditions?

options.explanation: Urea is partially reabsorbed and mostly excreted in urine.
Glucose is completely reabsorbed in the PCT under normal conditions.
Creatinine is a waste product that is not reabsorbed and is excreted in urine.
Uric acid is partially reabsorbed and secreted, but not completely reabsorbed.

questions.explanation: Under normal physiological conditions, glucose is completely reabsorbed from the glomerular filtrate in the Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) via active transport, provided its concentration does not exceed the renal threshold. Urea, creatinine, and uric acid are waste products that are either partially reabsorbed or secreted.
questions.hint: This substance is a primary energy source for cells and is reabsorbed actively in the PCT.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: If the efferent arteriole constricts while the afferent arteriole remains unchanged, what would be the immediate effect on the Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)?

options.explanation: Constriction of the efferent arteriole increases GFR, not decreases it.
The change in resistance alters the hydrostatic pressure, affecting GFR.
Increased resistance in the efferent arteriole raises glomerular hydrostatic pressure, increasing GFR.

options.text: GFR would first decrease, then increase
options.explanation: The effect is immediate and consistent, not a two-phase change.

questions.explanation: Constriction of the efferent arteriole increases the resistance to blood flow out of the glomerulus. This leads to a build-up of blood and a rise in glomerular hydrostatic pressure within the capillaries, which directly increases the net filtration pressure and consequently, the Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR).
questions.hint: Consider the effect of increased resistance on blood pressure within the glomerulus.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Arrange the following parts of the nephron in the correct sequence through which the filtrate passes during urine formation: I. Collecting Duct, II. Descending limb of Loop of Henle, III. Bowman's Capsule, IV. Ascending limb of Loop of Henle, V. Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT), VI. Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)

options.text: III -> VI -> II -> IV -> V -> I
options.explanation: This is the correct sequence of filtrate flow through the nephron.

options.text: III -> VI -> II -> IV -> V -> I
options.explanation: This option is identical to option A and is incorrect as a distinct choice.

options.text: III -> V -> VI -> II -> IV -> I
options.explanation: The sequence places DCT before PCT, which is incorrect.

options.text: III -> VI -> IV -> II -> V -> I
options.explanation: The sequence incorrectly places the ascending limb before the descending limb.

questions.explanation: The correct sequence of filtrate flow is: Bowman's Capsule (III) -> Proximal Convoluted Tubule (VI) -> Descending limb of Loop of Henle (II) -> Ascending limb of Loop of Henle (IV) -> Distal Convoluted Tubule (V) -> Collecting Duct (I).
questions.hint: Start from the initial filtration site and follow the path of filtrate through reabsorption and concentration.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) primarily acts on which two parts of the nephron to regulate water reabsorption?

options.text: Proximal Convoluted Tubule and Loop of Henle
options.explanation: ADH does not primarily act on these parts for water reabsorption.

options.text: Loop of Henle and Bowman's Capsule
options.explanation: ADH does not act on the Loop of Henle or Bowman's Capsule for water reabsorption.

options.text: Distal Convoluted Tubule and Collecting Duct
options.explanation: ADH increases water permeability in the DCT and Collecting Duct.
ADH does not act on the glomerulus or PCT for water reabsorption.

questions.explanation: ADH (Vasopressin) increases the permeability of the walls of the Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT) and the Collecting Duct to water. This increased permeability allows more water to be reabsorbed from the filtrate back into the blood, leading to the production of concentrated urine and conservation of body water.
questions.hint: ADH increases water reabsorption in the later parts of the nephron.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A person has a Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) of 125 mL/min and a Renal Plasma Flow (RPF) of 625 mL/min. What is the approximate filtration fraction (FF) for this person?

options.explanation: 10% would correspond to a GFR of 62.5 mL/min for the given RPF.
25% would correspond to a GFR of 156.25 mL/min for the given RPF.
30% would correspond to a GFR of 187.5 mL/min for the given RPF.

questions.explanation: The Filtration Fraction (FF) is calculated as the ratio of Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) to Renal Plasma Flow (RPF). FF = GFR / RPF = 125 mL/min / 625 mL/min = 0.2 or 20%.
questions.hint: Filtration fraction is the proportion of plasma flowing through the glomerulus that is filtered into the nephron.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the countercurrent mechanism in the human kidney is INCORRECT?

options.text: The descending limb of the Loop of Henle is permeable to water but impermeable to electrolytes.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The ascending limb of the Loop of Henle is impermeable to water but actively transports electrolytes out.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The vasa recta maintains the concentration gradient created by the Loop of Henle.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: Urea recycling from the collecting duct into the ascending limb of Loop of Henle contributes to the medullary interstitial gradient.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because urea recycling occurs into the descending limb, not the ascending limb.

questions.explanation: Urea recycling does contribute significantly to maintaining the medullary interstitial osmotic gradient, but it is reabsorbed from the collecting duct into the medullary interstitium and then diffuses into the *descending limb* of the Loop of Henle, not the ascending limb. The ascending limb is impermeable to urea.
questions.hint: Focus on the direction of urea movement and the permeability characteristics of the Loop of Henle limbs.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of the Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)?

options.text: Lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium.
options.explanation: This is a characteristic feature of the PCT.

options.text: Site of nearly complete reabsorption of essential nutrients.
options.explanation: This is a characteristic feature of the PCT.

options.text: Active secretion of H+ ions and ammonia into the filtrate.
options.explanation: This is a characteristic feature of the PCT.

options.text: Largely impermeable to water, leading to dilute filtrate.
options.explanation: The PCT is highly permeable to water, making this statement incorrect.

questions.explanation: The Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) is highly permeable to water. Approximately 70-80% of electrolytes and water are reabsorbed here, making it iso-osmotic with the plasma. The statement that it is largely impermeable to water is incorrect; this characteristic is more typical of the ascending limb of the Loop of Henle.
questions.hint: Consider the primary functions and permeability characteristics of the PCT.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A patient's urine sample shows the presence of glucose, even though their blood glucose level is within the normal range (below 180 mg/dL). Which of the following conditions is MOST likely indicated?

options.explanation: Diabetes mellitus involves high blood glucose levels, leading to glucosuria.
Excessive ADH affects water reabsorption, not glucose.
This condition leads to glucosuria despite normal blood glucose levels.

options.text: Glomerular damage leading to increased filtration of glucose
options.explanation: Glomerular damage would increase filtration of all small molecules, not just glucose.

questions.explanation: The renal threshold for glucose is typically around 180 mg/dL. If glucose is found in the urine (glucosuria) while blood glucose is normal, it suggests that the kidney tubules are unable to reabsorb glucose efficiently, even at normal concentrations. This points towards impaired tubular reabsorption, often due to a defect in the glucose transporters (e.g., renal glucosuria), rather than diabetes mellitus (which involves high blood glucose) or glomerular damage (which would increase filtration of all small molecules). Excessive ADH secretion would affect water reabsorption, not glucose.
questions.hint: Consider conditions that affect glucose reabsorption in the kidneys independently of blood glucose levels.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The Juxtaglomerular Apparatus (JGA) is a specialized sensitive region formed by the cellular modifications in the:

options.text: Proximal Convoluted Tubule and afferent arteriole
options.explanation: The JGA is not formed by the PCT and afferent arteriole.

options.text: Distal Convoluted Tubule and afferent arteriole
options.explanation: The JGA is formed by the DCT and afferent arteriole.
The JGA is not formed by the collecting duct and efferent arteriole.

options.text: Loop of Henle and efferent arteriole
options.explanation: The JGA is not formed by the Loop of Henle and efferent arteriole.

questions.explanation: The Juxtaglomerular Apparatus (JGA) is formed at the point of contact between the Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT) and the afferent arteriole of the same nephron. It consists of the macula densa cells of the DCT and the juxtaglomerular cells (JG cells) of the afferent arteriole, playing a crucial role in regulating GFR and blood pressure.
questions.hint: The JGA involves the distal part of the nephron and the afferent arteriole.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following structures constitutes the filtration barrier in the renal corpuscle?

options.text: Endothelium of afferent arteriole, basement membrane, podocytes
options.explanation: The endothelium of the afferent arteriole is not part of the filtration barrier; the correct endothelium is of the glomerular capillaries.

options.text: Endothelium of efferent arteriole, mesangial cells, podocytes
options.explanation: The endothelium of the efferent arteriole and mesangial cells are not part of the filtration barrier.

options.text: Podocytes, basement membrane, endothelium of glomerular capillaries
options.explanation: This is the correct combination forming the filtration barrier in the renal corpuscle.

options.text: Juxtaglomerular cells, macula densa, basement membrane
options.explanation: Juxtaglomerular cells and macula densa are not part of the filtration barrier.

questions.explanation: The filtration barrier (or glomerular filter) is formed by three layers: the endothelium of the glomerular blood vessels, the basement membrane between the endothelium and podocytes, and the podocytes (epithelial cells of Bowman's capsule) with their foot processes (pedicels).
questions.hint: Consider the layers involved in the filtration process in the glomerulus.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A patient presents with glycosuria despite normal blood glucose levels. Analysis of their kidney function reveals impaired reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubules. Which part of the nephron is most likely affected?

options.text: Ascending limb of Loop of Henle
options.explanation: The ascending limb of the Loop of Henle is not involved in glucose reabsorption.
The DCT is not the primary site for glucose reabsorption.
The PCT is responsible for 100% of glucose reabsorption under normal conditions.
The collecting duct is not involved in glucose reabsorption.

questions.explanation: The Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) is the primary site for the reabsorption of essential nutrients like glucose, amino acids, and vitamins. Under normal physiological conditions, 100% of filtered glucose is reabsorbed in the PCT. Impaired reabsorption of glucose, even with normal blood levels, strongly indicates a defect in the PCT's transport mechanisms.
questions.hint: Recall the primary site for glucose reabsorption in the nephron.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The maximum reabsorption of water (about 70-80% of filtrate) occurs in which segment of the nephron?

options.explanation: The DCT reabsorbs water but not the maximum amount.
The collecting duct reabsorbs water but not the maximum amount.
The Loop of Henle reabsorbs water but not the maximum amount.
The PCT reabsorbs about 70-80% of the filtrate's water.

questions.explanation: The Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) is responsible for the reabsorption of nearly all essential nutrients, 70-80% of electrolytes, and a significant amount (about 70-80%) of water from the glomerular filtrate. This reabsorption is obligatory and occurs regardless of the body's hydration state.
questions.hint: Think about the segment of the nephron where the majority of water reabsorption takes place.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: If the Glomerular Hydrostatic Pressure (GHP) is 60 mmHg, Blood Colloid Osmotic Pressure (BCOP) is 30 mmHg, and Capsular Hydrostatic Pressure (CHP) is 15 mmHg, what is the Net Filtration Pressure (NFP)?

options.explanation: The calculation yields NFP = 15 mmHg.
This is the sum of BCOP and CHP, not the NFP.
This is the sum of GHP and BCOP, not the NFP.
This is the sum of all three pressures, not the NFP.

questions.explanation: Net Filtration Pressure (NFP) is calculated using the formula: NFP = GHP - (BCOP + CHP). Given: GHP = 60 mmHg, BCOP = 30 mmHg, CHP = 15 mmHg. NFP = 60 mmHg - (30 mmHg + 15 mmHg) = 15 mmHg.
questions.hint: Use the formula for Net Filtration Pressure: NFP = GHP - (BCOP + CHP).
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A person suffers a severe hemorrhage, leading to a significant drop in blood volume and blood pressure. Which of the following physiological responses would occur to help restore blood volume and pressure, and how would it affect urine output?

options.text: Increased ADH secretion, leading to increased water reabsorption and concentrated urine.
options.explanation: ADH increases water reabsorption in the kidneys, reducing urine output and concentrating urine to restore blood volume and pressure.

options.text: Decreased ADH secretion, leading to increased water excretion and dilute urine.
options.explanation: Decreased ADH would increase urine output, worsening blood volume loss.

options.text: Increased aldosterone secretion, leading to increased sodium reabsorption and dilute urine.
options.explanation: Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption but does not directly affect urine concentration.

options.text: Decreased aldosterone secretion, leading to decreased sodium reabsorption and concentrated urine.
options.explanation: Decreased aldosterone would reduce sodium reabsorption, affecting blood pressure but not urine concentration directly.

questions.explanation: In response to severe hemorrhage, the body increases ADH (antidiuretic hormone) secretion to promote water reabsorption in the kidneys, reducing urine output and conserving water to restore blood volume and pressure.
questions.hint: Consider the hormonal response to low blood volume and its effect on urine concentration.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The primary function of the Bowman's capsule in the nephron is:

options.text: Secretion of hydrogen ions into the filtrate
options.explanation: Secretion of hydrogen ions occurs in the distal tubules and collecting ducts, not in Bowman's capsule.

options.text: Selective reabsorption of glucose and amino acids
options.explanation: Selective reabsorption primarily occurs in the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT), not Bowman's capsule.

options.text: Filtration of blood to form ultrafiltrate
options.explanation: Bowman's capsule filters blood from the glomerulus to form the ultrafiltrate.

options.text: Concentration of urine by water reabsorption
options.explanation: Concentration of urine occurs in the loop of Henle and collecting ducts, not Bowman's capsule.

questions.explanation: Bowman's capsule, along with the glomerulus, forms the renal corpuscle, which is the initial site of urine formation where blood is filtered under pressure to produce the glomerular filtrate (ultrafiltrate).
questions.hint: Consider the role of Bowman's capsule in the initial stage of urine formation.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which segment of the nephron is primarily responsible for the reabsorption of nearly all essential nutrients, such as glucose and amino acids, and 70-80% of electrolytes and water?

options.explanation: The loop of Henle is primarily involved in creating a concentration gradient, not reabsorption of nutrients.
The DCT is involved in fine-tuning reabsorption and secretion but not the primary reabsorption of nutrients.
The collecting duct is mainly involved in water reabsorption under ADH influence, not nutrient reabsorption.
The PCT reabsorbs nearly all essential nutrients, electrolytes, and water from the filtrate.

questions.explanation: The Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) is highly permeable and equipped with numerous microvilli and mitochondria, making it the primary site for the reabsorption of most valuable substances and a significant portion of water and electrolytes from the glomerular filtrate.
questions.hint: Think about the segment of the nephron with the highest reabsorptive capacity.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: If the levels of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) in the body are significantly reduced, what would be the most likely effect on urine production?

options.text: Production of a small volume of highly concentrated urine
options.explanation: Low ADH leads to less water reabsorption, not more.

options.text: Production of a large volume of dilute urine
options.explanation: Low ADH reduces water reabsorption, resulting in dilute urine and increased urine volume.

options.text: No significant change in urine volume or concentration
options.explanation: ADH directly affects urine concentration and volume.

options.text: Increased reabsorption of sodium ions in the DCT
options.explanation: ADH does not directly affect sodium reabsorption; aldosterone does.

questions.explanation: ADH increases the permeability of the Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT) and collecting duct to water. Low ADH levels result in decreased water reabsorption in these segments, leading to more water being excreted and thus producing a large volume of dilute urine.
questions.hint: Consider the role of ADH in water reabsorption in the kidneys.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The presence of glucose in the urine (glycosuria) despite normal kidney function, typically indicates:

options.text: Efficient reabsorption of glucose in the Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)
options.explanation: Efficient reabsorption would prevent glycosuria, not cause it.

options.text: Normal physiological functioning of the renal tubules
options.explanation: Normal function would not result in glucose in urine unless the threshold is exceeded.

options.text: Blood glucose levels exceeding the renal threshold
options.explanation: Glycosuria occurs when blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold for reabsorption.

options.text: Increased secretion of ADH leading to excess water reabsorption
options.explanation: ADH affects water reabsorption, not glucose reabsorption.

questions.explanation: In healthy individuals, all filtered glucose is reabsorbed in the PCT. Glycosuria occurs when the blood glucose concentration is so high that the transport maximum (renal threshold) for glucose reabsorption in the PCT is exceeded, meaning the tubules cannot reabsorb all the filtered glucose.
questions.hint: Consider the renal threshold for glucose reabsorption.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The counter-current mechanism involving the Loop of Henle and vasa recta is crucial for which of the following functions in the kidney?

options.text: Facilitating the active transport of glucose and amino acids
options.explanation: Active transport of glucose and amino acids occurs in the PCT, not the counter-current mechanism.

options.text: Maintaining a steep osmotic gradient in the renal medulla
options.explanation: The counter-current mechanism maintains the osmotic gradient necessary for urine concentration.

options.text: Regulating blood pressure through renin secretion
options.explanation: Renin secretion regulates blood pressure but is not directly related to the counter-current mechanism.

options.text: Rapidly exchanging gases between blood and filtrate
options.explanation: The counter-current mechanism does not involve gas exchange.

questions.explanation: The counter-current mechanism, through the opposing flows in the Loop of Henle and vasa recta, is essential for creating and maintaining a hyperosmotic environment in the renal medulla, which is vital for the concentration of urine under the influence of ADH.
questions.hint: Think about the role of the counter-current mechanism in urine concentration.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A patient's kidney exhibits a Glomerular Hydrostatic Pressure (GHP) of 60 mmHg, a Blood Colloidal Osmotic Pressure (BCOP) of 32 mmHg, and a Capsular Hydrostatic Pressure (CHP) of 18 mmHg. Calculate the Net Filtration Pressure (NFP).

options.explanation: This is the sum of GHP and BCOP + CHP, not the NFP.
This is GHP + CHP, not the NFP.
This is GHP - BCOP, not the correct NFP calculation.

questions.explanation: Net Filtration Pressure (NFP) is calculated as: NFP = GHP - (BCOP + CHP). Substituting the values: NFP = 60 mmHg - (32 mmHg + 18 mmHg) = 10 mmHg.
questions.hint: Use the formula NFP = GHP - (BCOP + CHP) to calculate the net filtration pressure.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: If a person consumes a large amount of sodium chloride, leading to an increase in blood volume and blood pressure, which of the following hormonal responses would primarily act to restore fluid balance and reduce blood pressure?

options.text: Increased secretion of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF)
options.explanation: ANF is released in response to high blood volume/pressure and promotes sodium and water excretion to reduce blood volume and pressure.
Decreased renin would reduce aldosterone, but ANF is the direct counter-regulatory hormone for excess volume/pressure.
Aldosterone promotes sodium and water reabsorption, which would increase blood volume and pressure, not reduce it.
Decreased ADH would reduce water reabsorption, but ANF is the primary hormone responding to high blood volume/pressure.

questions.explanation: High salt intake leads to increased blood volume and pressure. Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) is released by the atrial walls of the heart in response to increased blood volume and pressure. ANF promotes vasodilation and increased excretion of sodium and water by the kidneys, thereby decreasing blood volume and pressure, counteracting the effects of excess salt.
questions.hint: Consider the hormone that counteracts increased blood volume and pressure due to high salt intake.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of major processes involved in the formation of urine after the initial glomerular filtration?

options.explanation: This is not the correct sequence; reabsorption occurs before secretion and concentration.
This is the correct sequence: reabsorption first, then secretion, and finally concentration.
Concentration is the last step, not the first.
This is not the correct sequence; reabsorption occurs before secretion and concentration.

questions.explanation: After glomerular filtration, the filtrate undergoes selective reabsorption in the renal tubules, where useful substances are returned to the blood. Simultaneously, tubular secretion adds waste products from the blood into the filtrate. The final step, concentration of urine, occurs primarily in the Loop of Henle and collecting duct.
questions.hint: Consider the order of processes: reabsorption, secretion, and concentration.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following substances is almost completely reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule under normal physiological conditions, and its presence in urine indicates a pathology?

options.explanation: Urea is partially reabsorbed, not fully.
Creatinine is largely secreted, not reabsorbed.
Glucose is fully reabsorbed in the PCT; its presence in urine indicates pathology.
Hydrogen ions are secreted, not reabsorbed, in significant amounts in the PCT.

questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, glucose is completely reabsorbed from the filtrate in the PCT by active transport. Its presence in urine (glycosuria) usually indicates conditions like diabetes mellitus where blood glucose levels exceed the renal threshold.
questions.hint: Consider which substance is fully reabsorbed in the PCT and its presence in urine indicates a problem.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A patient suffering from diabetes insipidus would typically exhibit symptoms primarily related to:

options.text: Excessive thirst (polydipsia) and production of a large volume of dilute urine (polyuria)
options.explanation: These are the hallmark symptoms of diabetes insipidus due to impaired ADH function.

options.text: High blood glucose levels and presence of ketones in urine
options.explanation: These symptoms are associated with diabetes mellitus, not diabetes insipidus.

options.text: Significant presence of proteins in urine (proteinuria) and edema
options.explanation: These symptoms are associated with nephrotic syndrome or kidney disease.

options.text: Reduced glomerular filtration rate leading to accumulation of nitrogenous wastes
options.explanation: These symptoms are associated with chronic kidney disease, not diabetes insipidus.

questions.explanation: Diabetes insipidus is a condition caused by inadequate production of ADH or the kidneys' inability to respond to ADH. This results in impaired water reabsorption in the collecting ducts, leading to the excretion of a large volume of very dilute urine (polyuria) and compensatory excessive thirst (polydipsia).
questions.hint: Consider the primary symptoms of diabetes insipidus related to ADH deficiency.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary site of selective reabsorption during urine formation in the nephron?

options.explanation: The glomerulus is the site of filtration, not selective reabsorption.
Correct. The PCT is the primary site for selective reabsorption.
The Loop of Henle is involved in creating a concentration gradient but not the primary site for selective reabsorption.
The DCT is involved in fine-tuning reabsorption but not the primary site.

questions.explanation: The PCT is the primary site for selective reabsorption, where ~65% of filtered water, glucose, amino acids, and ions (like Na⁺ and Cl⁻) are reabsorbed back into the blood.
questions.hint: Consider the major functions of different parts of the nephron.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: If the glomerular capillary pressure is 50 mmHg, Bowman’s capsule pressure is 15 mmHg, and the colloid osmotic pressure is 25 mmHg, what is the net filtration pressure (NFP)?

options.explanation: Correct. The calculation yields 10 mmHg.
Incorrect. The calculation does not yield 20 mmHg.
Incorrect. The calculation does not yield 30 mmHg.
Incorrect. The calculation does not yield 40 mmHg.

questions.explanation: NFP = (Glomerular capillary pressure) – (Bowman’s capsule pressure + Colloid osmotic pressure) = 50 – (15 + 25) = 50 – 40 = 10 mmHg.
questions.hint: Use the formula for net filtration pressure: NFP = GCP - (BCP + COP).
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following substances is least likely to be reabsorbed in the nephron under normal physiological conditions?

options.explanation: Glucose is almost completely reabsorbed in the PCT.
Correct. Urea is only partially reabsorbed (~50%).
Sodium ions are almost completely reabsorbed.
Water is reabsorbed variably based on ADH levels.

questions.explanation: Urea undergoes passive reabsorption in the PCT and collecting ducts, but only ~50% is reabsorbed; glucose and sodium are almost completely reabsorbed, and water is reabsorbed variably based on ADH levels.
questions.hint: Consider the reabsorption efficiency of different substances in the nephron.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The process of tubular secretion primarily occurs in:

options.explanation: The glomerulus is the site of filtration, not secretion.
The PCT is primarily involved in reabsorption, not secretion.
The Loop of Henle is involved in creating a concentration gradient, not secretion.
Correct. Tubular secretion primarily occurs in the DCT and collecting ducts.

questions.explanation: Tubular secretion involves the active transport of substances like H⁺, K⁺, ammonia, and drugs from peritubular capillaries into the tubular lumen, mainly in the DCT and collecting ducts.
questions.hint: Consider the parts of the nephron involved in secretion.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A patient presents with a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 120 ml/min and a plasma creatinine concentration of 1.2 mg/dl. If the creatinine clearance is calculated as (urine concentration × urine flow rate) / plasma concentration, which of the following is the most likely urine flow rate if urine creatinine is 120 mg/dl and urine volume is 1.5 L/day?

options.explanation: Incorrect. The calculation does not yield 1 ml/min.
Correct. The calculation yields 1.2 ml/min.
Incorrect. The calculation does not yield 1.5 ml/min.
Incorrect. The calculation does not yield 2.0 ml/min.

questions.explanation: Creatinine clearance ≈ GFR = 120 ml/min. Creatinine clearance = (Urine creatinine × Urine flow rate) / Plasma creatinine. 120 = (120 × Urine flow rate) / 1.2 → Urine flow rate = (120 × 1.2) / 120 = 1.2 ml/min.
questions.hint: Use the creatinine clearance formula and convert units as necessary.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following hormones increases the reabsorption of water but decreases the reabsorption of sodium in the nephron?

options.explanation: Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion.
Correct. ADH increases water reabsorption but does not directly affect sodium reabsorption.
ANP decreases sodium reabsorption and increases urine output.
PTH primarily regulates calcium and phosphate reabsorption.

questions.explanation: ADH (vasopressin) increases water permeability in the collecting ducts via aquaporin-2 channels, leading to water reabsorption, but it does not directly affect sodium reabsorption.
questions.hint: Consider the primary functions of the hormones listed.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A defect in the Na⁺-K⁺-2Cl⁻ co-transporter (NKCC2) in the thick ascending limb of the Loop of Henle would most directly impair:

options.explanation: Glucose reabsorption occurs in the PCT and is not directly affected by NKCC2.
Water reabsorption is indirectly affected but not the primary impairment.
Correct. NKCC2 is essential for sodium reabsorption in the thick ascending limb.
Potassium secretion is affected but not the primary impairment.

questions.explanation: NKCC2 is essential for the reabsorption of Na⁺, K⁺, and Cl⁻ in the thick ascending limb. Its dysfunction would directly impair sodium reabsorption.
questions.hint: Consider the role of NKCC2 in ion transport.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The countercurrent multiplier system in the Loop of Henle primarily functions to:

options.text: Concentrate urine by creating a hyperosmotic medullary interstitium
options.explanation: Correct. The countercurrent multiplier system creates a hyperosmotic medullary interstitium.

options.text: Dilute urine by increasing water reabsorption in the PCT
options.explanation: The PCT is not the primary site for the countercurrent multiplier system.

options.text: Secrete H⁺ ions into the tubular lumen
options.explanation: H⁺ secretion occurs in the DCT and collecting ducts, not the Loop of Henle.

options.text: Filter plasma proteins into the glomerular capsule
options.explanation: Plasma proteins are not filtered into the glomerular capsule.

questions.explanation: The countercurrent multiplier system establishes a gradient of increasing osmolarity from the cortex to the medulla, enabling the kidneys to produce concentrated urine.
questions.hint: Consider the role of the countercurrent multiplier in urine concentration.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about facultative water reabsorption is correct?

options.text: It occurs primarily in the PCT
options.explanation: Facultative water reabsorption occurs in the DCT and collecting ducts.

options.text: It is independent of ADH levels
options.explanation: Facultative water reabsorption is dependent on ADH levels.

options.text: It accounts for ~10% of total water reabsorption
options.explanation: Correct. Facultative water reabsorption accounts for ~10% of total water reabsorption.
Facultative water reabsorption is regulated by ADH, not aldosterone.

questions.explanation: Facultative water reabsorption (~10% of total) occurs in the DCT and collecting ducts and is dependent on ADH levels, which regulate aquaporin-2 channels.
questions.hint: Consider the role of ADH in facultative water reabsorption.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A drug that inhibits carbonic anhydrase would most likely lead to:

options.text: Increased reabsorption of bicarbonate in the PCT
options.explanation: Correct. Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase reduces H⁺ secretion, leading to decreased bicarbonate reabsorption.
Glucose reabsorption is not directly affected by carbonic anhydrase inhibition.
Potassium secretion is not directly affected by carbonic anhydrase inhibition.
Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase reduces H⁺ secretion, but this is not the primary effect described.

questions.explanation: Carbonic anhydrase is crucial for the conversion of CO₂ and H₂O to H₂CO₃, which dissociates into H⁺ and HCO₃⁻. Inhibition reduces H⁺ secretion, leading to decreased bicarbonate reabsorption in the PCT.
questions.hint: Consider the role of carbonic anhydrase in bicarbonate reabsorption.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following components is *not* a part of the glomerular filtration membrane?

options.explanation: This is a part of the glomerular filtration membrane.

options.text: Basement membrane between endothelium and podocytes
options.explanation: This is a part of the glomerular filtration membrane.
This is a part of the glomerular filtration membrane.
Juxtaglomerular cells are part of the juxtaglomerular apparatus, not the filtration membrane.

questions.explanation: The glomerular filtration membrane consists of three layers: the endothelium of the glomerular blood vessels, the basement membrane (a thin layer between the endothelium and the podocytes), and the podocytes (epithelial cells of Bowman's capsule with filtration slits). Juxtaglomerular cells are part of the juxtaglomerular apparatus, involved in the regulation of glomerular filtration rate and blood pressure, but not directly part of the filtration barrier itself.
questions.hint: Consider the components involved in the filtration barrier of the glomerulus.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The countercurrent mechanism primarily operates to:

options.text: Actively transport glucose and amino acids out of the nephron.
options.explanation: The countercurrent mechanism does not primarily transport glucose and amino acids.

options.text: Facilitate the secretion of hydrogen ions and potassium into the filtrate.
options.explanation: This is not the primary function of the countercurrent mechanism.

options.text: Maintain a steep osmotic gradient in the medullary interstitium.
options.explanation: This is the primary function of the countercurrent mechanism.

options.text: Increase the glomerular filtration rate by dilating the afferent arteriole.
options.explanation: This is not the primary function of the countercurrent mechanism.

questions.explanation: The countercurrent mechanism, involving the Loop of Henle and the vasa recta, is crucial for maintaining a high and progressively increasing osmotic gradient (from 300 mOsmol/L in the cortex to about 1200 mOsmol/L in the inner medulla) in the medullary interstitium. This gradient is essential for the kidney's ability to produce concentrated urine by allowing water reabsorption from the collecting duct.
questions.hint: Think about the role of the countercurrent mechanism in urine concentration.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A patient presents with symptoms of polyuria (excessive urination) and polydipsia (excessive thirst), but normal blood glucose levels. Analysis of their urine shows very dilute urine (low osmolality). Which of the following conditions is most likely indicated?

options.explanation: Diabetes mellitus is characterized by high blood glucose levels.
Glomerulonephritis typically involves protein or blood in urine, not dilute urine.
Diabetes insipidus is characterized by the inability to produce or respond to ADH, leading to dilute urine.
Renal calculi cause pain and obstruction, not primarily dilute urine or polyuria/polydipsia.

questions.explanation: The key symptoms are polyuria and polydipsia with *normal blood glucose*, and *dilute urine*. Diabetes mellitus is ruled out by normal blood glucose. Glomerulonephritis would typically involve protein or blood in urine, not necessarily dilute urine. Renal calculi (kidney stones) cause pain and obstruction, not primarily dilute urine or polyuria/polydipsia without other symptoms. Diabetes insipidus is characterized by the inability to produce or respond to ADH (vasopressin), leading to impaired water reabsorption in the collecting ducts and DCT, resulting in the excretion of large volumes of dilute urine and compensatory thirst.
questions.hint: Consider conditions that cause polyuria and polydipsia with normal blood glucose.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) or vasopressin primarily acts on which part of the nephron to increase water reabsorption?

options.explanation: ADH does not primarily act on the PCT.
ADH does not primarily act on the ascending limb of Henle's loop.
ADH does not primarily act on the descending limb of Henle's loop.

options.text: Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT) and Collecting Duct
options.explanation: ADH primarily acts on the DCT and collecting duct to increase water reabsorption.

questions.explanation: ADH (Vasopressin) primarily acts on the principal cells of the distal convoluted tubule (DCT) and the collecting duct. It increases their permeability to water by stimulating the insertion of aquaporin-2 channels into the apical membrane, thereby promoting water reabsorption and leading to the formation of concentrated urine.
questions.hint: Consider the parts of the nephron involved in water reabsorption under hormonal influence.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: If the Glomerular Hydrostatic Pressure (GHP) is 60 mmHg, the Blood Colloid Osmotic Pressure (BCOP) is 30 mmHg, and the Capsular Hydrostatic Pressure (CHP) is 15 mmHg, what is the Net Filtration Pressure (NFP)?

options.explanation: This is the correct value, but it is listed twice, which is incorrect.
This is the correct value for NFP.
This is not the correct value for NFP.
This is not the correct value for NFP.

questions.explanation: The Net Filtration Pressure (NFP) is calculated as: NFP = GHP - (BCOP + CHP) = 60 mmHg - (30 mmHg + 15 mmHg) = 15 mmHg. This positive value indicates a net movement of fluid out of the glomerulus into Bowman's capsule.
questions.hint: Use the formula for Net Filtration Pressure: NFP = GHP - (BCOP + CHP).
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the sequence of events in the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) activation?

options.text: Angiotensinogen → Angiotensin II → Renin → Aldosterone secretion
options.explanation: This is not the correct sequence.

options.text: Decreased GFR → Aldosterone secretion → Angiotensin I → Renin
options.explanation: This is not the correct sequence.

options.text: Renin release → Angiotensinogen conversion to Angiotensin I → Angiotensin I conversion to Angiotensin II → Aldosterone secretion
options.explanation: This is the correct sequence of events in the RAAS activation.

options.text: Angiotensin II → ACE release → Renin release → Vasoconstriction
options.explanation: This is not the correct sequence.

questions.explanation: The correct sequence is: When GFR or blood pressure drops, the juxtaglomerular cells release **Renin**. Renin acts on **Angiotensinogen** (produced by the liver) to convert it into **Angiotensin I**. Angiotensin I is then converted to **Angiotensin II** by Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE), primarily in the lungs. Angiotensin II is a potent vasoconstrictor and stimulates the adrenal cortex to secrete **Aldosterone**, which increases Na+ and water reabsorption.
questions.hint: Consider the sequence of hormone and enzyme interactions in the RAAS pathway.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which section of the nephron is almost entirely impermeable to water, regardless of hormonal influence, and plays a crucial role in diluting the filtrate?

options.explanation: The PCT is permeable to water.

options.text: Ascending limb of the Loop of Henle
options.explanation: The ascending limb is impermeable to water and plays a crucial role in diluting the filtrate.

options.text: Descending limb of the Loop of Henle
options.explanation: The descending limb is permeable to water.
The collecting duct is permeable to water under the influence of ADH.

questions.explanation: The ascending limb of the Loop of Henle is characterized by its impermeability to water. It actively transports Na+, K+, and Cl- ions out of the filtrate into the medullary interstitium, but water cannot follow due to the impermeability of its walls. This action causes the filtrate to become progressively more dilute as it moves up the ascending limb.
questions.hint: Consider the parts of the nephron involved in diluting the filtrate.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A person is stranded in a desert with severe dehydration. Which of the following physiological responses would be expected regarding their urine formation?

options.text: Decreased ADH release, leading to increased urine volume and dilute urine.
options.explanation: This would not conserve water in dehydration.

options.text: Increased GFR to excrete more waste, resulting in increased urine volume.
options.explanation: Increased GFR is not a typical response to dehydration.

options.text: Decreased reabsorption of water in the collecting duct, leading to dilute urine.
options.explanation: This would not conserve water in dehydration.

options.text: Increased ADH release, leading to increased water reabsorption and concentrated urine.
options.explanation: This is the body's response to conserve water during dehydration.

questions.explanation: In severe dehydration, the body's osmoreceptors detect an increase in blood osmolality. This stimulates the posterior pituitary to release a higher amount of ADH. Increased ADH acts on the DCT and collecting ducts, making them more permeable to water, thus increasing water reabsorption back into the blood. This results in the formation of a smaller volume of highly concentrated urine, conserving water for the body.
questions.hint: Consider the body's response to severe dehydration and its effect on urine concentration.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The micturition reflex is primarily a neural reflex that involves:

options.text: Only voluntary control of the external urethral sphincter.
options.explanation: The reflex involves both involuntary and voluntary components.

options.text: Only involuntary contraction of the detrusor muscle.
options.explanation: The reflex involves both involuntary and voluntary components.

options.text: Both involuntary contraction of the detrusor muscle and voluntary relaxation of the external urethral sphincter.
options.explanation: This is the correct description of the micturition reflex.

options.text: Active transport of urine out of the bladder.
options.explanation: The micturition reflex does not involve active transport of urine.

questions.explanation: The micturition reflex is a spinal reflex. As the bladder fills, stretch receptors send signals to the spinal cord. This initiates an involuntary reflex arc that causes contraction of the detrusor muscle (bladder wall) and relaxation of the internal urethral sphincter. While this is an involuntary reflex, the external urethral sphincter is under voluntary control, allowing an individual to consciously initiate or delay urination.
questions.hint: Consider the neural and muscular components involved in the micturition reflex.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following substances is *almost completely* reabsorbed from the filtrate in a healthy individual under normal physiological conditions?

options.explanation: Urea is partially reabsorbed.
Creatinine is not reabsorbed.
Glucose is almost completely reabsorbed in the PCT.
Uric acid is partially reabsorbed.

questions.explanation: In a healthy individual, glucose is almost completely reabsorbed from the filtrate in the Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) via active transport, assuming blood glucose levels are within the normal range and the transport maximum for glucose is not exceeded. Urea, creatinine, and uric acid are waste products that are either partially reabsorbed or secreted, but not completely reabsorbed like glucose.
questions.hint: Consider substances that are typically reabsorbed completely in the nephron.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which part of the nephron is primarily responsible for the obligatory reabsorption of approximately 70-80% of electrolytes and water, along with nearly 100% of glucose and amino acids?

options.explanation: The glomerulus is responsible for filtration, not reabsorption.
The Loop of Henle is involved in creating a concentration gradient but not bulk reabsorption.
Correct. The PCT reabsorbs 70-80% of electrolytes and water, and nearly 100% of glucose and amino acids.
The DCT is involved in facultative reabsorption, not bulk reabsorption.

questions.explanation: The Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) is the primary site for the bulk of reabsorption of essential substances like glucose, amino acids, and a large proportion of electrolytes and water. This reabsorption is largely obligatory, meaning it occurs continuously regardless of the body's hydration state.
questions.hint: Consider the role of different nephron segments in reabsorption.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A patient presents with symptoms indicating a defect in the kidney's ability to concentrate urine effectively. Which of the following scenarios would most directly impair the establishment of a hyperosmolar medullary interstitial gradient, crucial for urine concentration?

options.text: Increased permeability of the descending limb of the Loop of Henle to water.
options.explanation: Increased permeability of the descending limb to water does not impair the gradient; it may even enhance it.

options.text: Impaired active transport of Na+ and Cl- out of the ascending limb of the Loop of Henle.
options.explanation: Correct. Active transport of Na+ and Cl- in the ascending limb is critical for establishing the hyperosmolar medullary gradient.

options.text: Decreased reabsorption of bicarbonate ions in the Proximal Convoluted Tubule.
options.explanation: Bicarbonate reabsorption in the PCT does not directly affect the medullary gradient.

options.text: Reduced secretion of H+ ions into the filtrate in the Distal Convoluted Tubule.
options.explanation: H+ secretion in the DCT does not directly impact the medullary gradient.

questions.explanation: The ascending limb of the Loop of Henle actively transports Na+ and Cl- ions out into the medullary interstitium, establishing the hyperosmolar gradient essential for urine concentration.
questions.hint: Focus on the role of the Loop of Henle in creating the medullary gradient.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: If the glomerular hydrostatic pressure (GHP) is 60 mmHg, Bowman's capsular hydrostatic pressure (BCHP) is 18 mmHg, and glomerular colloid osmotic pressure (GCOP) is 32 mmHg, what is the Net Filtration Pressure (NFP) responsible for ultrafiltration in the glomerulus?

options.explanation: Correct. NFP = 60 - (18 + 32) = 10 mmHg.
Incorrect. This value does not match the calculated NFP.
Incorrect. This value is the sum of BCHP and GCOP, not the NFP.
Incorrect. This value exceeds the given pressures and is not the NFP.

questions.explanation: Net Filtration Pressure (NFP) is calculated as GHP - (BCHP + GCOP). Substituting the values: 60 - (18 + 32) = 10 mmHg.
questions.hint: Use the formula NFP = GHP - (BCHP + GCOP).
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A healthy individual consumes a large volume of water rapidly. Which of the following physiological responses would not be expected in their renal system shortly after this event?

options.text: Decreased release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) from the posterior pituitary.
options.explanation: This is expected after rapid water intake due to decreased plasma osmolality.

options.text: Increased number of aquaporin channels inserted into the apical membrane of collecting duct cells.
options.explanation: Correct. This response would not occur; instead, fewer aquaporin channels are inserted.

options.text: Production of a larger volume of dilute (hypotonic) urine.
options.explanation: This is expected due to reduced water reabsorption.

options.text: Decreased reabsorption of water from the collecting ducts.
options.explanation: This is expected due to reduced ADH and aquaporin channels.

questions.explanation: After rapid water intake, ADH release decreases, leading to fewer aquaporin channels in the collecting duct, making it less permeable to water. Thus, an increase in aquaporin channels would not occur.
questions.hint: Consider the role of ADH in water reabsorption.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following substances, if found in significant amounts in the urine of a healthy individual, would most strongly indicate a failure in the reabsorption mechanism of the Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)?

options.explanation: Urea is a waste product and is normally present in urine; some is reabsorbed in the PCT.
Creatinine is a waste product and is not reabsorbed in the PCT.
Correct. Glucose is normally 100% reabsorbed in the PCT; its presence in urine indicates a failure in reabsorption.
Potassium ions are reabsorbed and secreted in the DCT and collecting duct, not primarily in the PCT.

questions.explanation: Glucose is almost completely reabsorbed in the PCT under normal conditions. Its presence in urine (glycosuria) indicates a failure in PCT reabsorption, often due to diabetes mellitus or a low renal threshold.
questions.hint: Consider which substances are normally fully reabsorbed in the PCT.
questions.subject: neet-zoology
